papers_read.title_as_printed: Deep learning-based classification of healthy aging controls, mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease using fusion of MRI-PET imaging (Rallabandi & Seetharaman, 2023, doi 10.1016/j.bspc.2022.104312, file S1746809422007662)

Analysis of neuropsychological and neuroradiological features for diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease and mild cognitive impairment (Kurbalija et al., International Journal of Medical Informatics 178 (2023) 105195)

what_each_reports.P-117: The record's P-117 (summaries.md S1746809423005462: resting-state EEG, VMD + NSGA-II, best ~99.8% accuracy, sample not reported) could not be checked; the pack PDF is a different paper (OASIS MRI-PET fusion, 95.5% HC vs MCI, AUC 0.988).
what_each_reports.P-95: Seven Weka classifiers on 482 neuropsychological + neuroradiological features, 90 Novi Sad participants (30 AD, 30 MCI, 30 controls), THREE-class AD/MCI/control classification, 10x10 stratified CV. Accuracy with all attributes 66.22% (LR) to 81.00% (naive Bayes); weighted AUROC 76.3-95.0%.

quantity_a: Record's P-117: EEG classifier accuracy, binary MCI vs healthy, own cohort, internal validation (summary block only).
quantity_b: P-95: three-class (AD/MCI/control) accuracy across seven classifiers, 90 participants, neuropsychological + MRI features, 10x10 CV.
incompatible_if_same: Not applicable: a three-class accuracy range across seven classifiers is not the same estimand as a binary accuracy; chance level alone differs (33% vs 50%).

gates.task: mismatch: P-95 is three-class AD/MCI/control (registry T3), not the binary MCI vs control task the record assigns
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: Novi Sad clinical cohort vs P-117's EEG cohort (or OASIS); record's dataset_equal='Yes' unsupported
gates.modality_family: mismatch: neuropsychological tests + structural/diffusion MRI vs EEG; no waiver on record

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: three-class accuracy range vs binary accuracy
performance_validity: Likely applies to P-117 (claimed 99.81% internal) but unconfirmable without the correct PDF; not needed for the verdict.
grounds: The supplied P-117 PDF is the wrong paper (OASIS MRI-PET fusion), so the 99.81% EEG result cannot be checked from source.
P-95's 66-81% is a three-class AD/MCI/control accuracy range across seven classifiers, so the task gate fails and the endpoint differs from a binary MCI vs control accuracy.
The dataset-family and modality-family gates also fail, with no waiver on record.

evidence_quotes.quote: taken from Open Access Series of Imaging Studies (OASIS) online dataset
Reported best performance near **99.8%** using optimized subset + ensemble setup.
Results: The accuracy for the whole set of attributes ranged between 66.22 % and 81.00 %, and the weighted average AUROC was between 76.3 % and 95.0 %.
the application of machine learning techniques in AD diagnosis will be directed toward the creation of ML classifiers which will be trained to perform the 3-class classification.
The data includes neuroradiological (NR) and neuropsychological (NP) parameters of 90 people, divided into three different groups of equal sizes (per 30 participants)

record_defects: P-117's paper_pdf_map entry points to the wrong PDF (MRI-PET S1746809422007662 instead of EEG S1746809423005462).
task_equal='Yes' and claim_b '66-81% on T1' are wrong: P-95's figure is a three-class AD/MCI/control accuracy (registry itself codes T3).
Registry row P-117: Best_Metric and Dataset 'not reported' despite the 99.81% claim.
resolution_note's bridging list is boilerplate unrelated to either paper.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing plausible: the three-class endpoint makes P-95 incommensurable with a binary accuracy regardless of the correct P-117 PDF.
